solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Method of very quietly feeding a fish

indicators.note: feeding something means putting it into a mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish; the article is kept as A
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: An angler describes a technique for baiting a fish without making noise.
explanation.walkthrough: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet; the fish has to be read with its article attached.
explanation.definitionFit: An approach is a way of tackling something, a synonym for a method or technique.

clue.text: Doctor photographs strain and graze

parts.note: a strain is a tune or melody, as is an air
to graze is to touch lightly in passing, to brush

explanation.surface: A medical doctor examines X-rays, a sprain and a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor is a verb here, meaning to falsify, not a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush images is to retouch them, which is a way of falsifying or doctoring pictures.

clue.text: Stop meeting hooker, reprobate!

parts.note: pro is slang for a prostitute
a rogue is a scoundrel or reprobate

explanation.surface: An outraged cry to a scoundrel to stop seeing a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue a parliament is to discontinue its session without dissolving it, halting its sittings.

clue.text: Run around, trapped by unusually big predators

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so these letters go within what follows

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, an unusually large garment size
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
ca, circa, means around

explanation.surface: An animal flees around the area but is caught by large hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually does not signal an anagram here; it is the clothing label OS, outsize. Big serves both as part of the definition and to give a fair reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcas, killer whales, are apex hunters of the ocean that kill seals and even sharks.

clue.text: It combats the cold charm heartlessly used in infidelity

indicators.note: used in means put inside, so the trimmed word goes within the next one

parts.note: cheating is infidelity to a partner

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is removed

parts.note: to charm is to enthral

explanation.surface: Something that fights off a chill uses heartless charm in an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, and the trimmed word sits just after the opening letter of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A central heating system warms a whole building from one boiler, keeping out winter chill.

clue.text: Switch feet from right to left

indicators.note: reading from right to left is reading the word backwards in an across entry

parts.note: animals' feet are paws

explanation.surface: Someone changes which foot leads, moving from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap is to exchange one thing for another, a synonym for switch as a verb.

clue.text: Spirit of one consumed by rage

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so this goes inside the next word

parts.note: wrath is great anger
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Describes the spirit of someone eaten up with fury.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or apparition, a synonym for a spirit of the dead.

clue.text: Not worth having drink after uplift on tax

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up means reading from the bottom upward

parts.note: to lap is to drink as an animal does
to tax someone's patience is to try it

explanation.surface: Something is not worth it once a tax increase is added to the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something paltry is trivial or meagre, too small to be of any value.

clue.text: Harp on a floor's edge had to be moved

indicators.note: letters that have to be moved are shifted into new positions

parts.note: taken as written, with the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: An instrument on the edge of a floor needed moving.
explanation.walkthrough: Harp looks like the instrument, but harp on is a phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To flog a dead horse is to keep pursuing a hopeless point, like going on and on about something.

clue.text: Waste product's first to go after a flush

indicators.note: the first letter goes, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
effluent is liquid waste

explanation.surface: Sewage is the first thing to disappear when a toilet is flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Flush here is the adjective meaning having plenty of money, not the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means wealthy, and flush is informal for having plenty of cash.

clue.text: Spread coal tar on canine's sensitive area

indicators.note: something spread is laid out loosely, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone daubs coal tar on a dog's sore spot as a home remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The canine is not a dog but a canine tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The root canal is the pulp-filled channel inside a tooth's root, where nerves make it tender.

clue.text: Thrash sides in financial trouble

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its two outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A company thrashes about on both fronts while in money difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail is to thrash about wildly or to beat, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Cons finally ask to wear jumpers

indicators.note: something worn is surrounded by its wearer, so it goes inside

parts.note: roos, kangaroos, are famous jumpers

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the next word

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Convicts are asked to put on sweaters in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumpers looks like sweaters (a British jumper is a pullover) but here means kangaroos.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is to swindle or cheat them, so rooks is the verb cons.

clue.text: Device for controlling temperature in our lager supply

indicators.note: in places one letter within the following words before the mixing
read as supple-y, i.e. bent and pliable, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the standard abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A pub needs a gadget to keep the temperature of its beer supply right.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a mechanism that keeps a quantity such as heat, flow or pressure at a set level.

clue.text: Drink to lacrosse's first summer league table

parts.note: squash is a fruit cordial diluted with water

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter of the word
read as sum-mer, one who sums, i.e. an adder

explanation.surface: A drink is raised to the leaders of the summer lacrosse league.
explanation.walkthrough: Summer is not the season but someone who does sums. Squash is a British soft drink made by diluting a fruit concentrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A squash ladder is a club ranking where players climb by challenging those above, a kind of league table.

clue.text: Whiffs of fish start to escape aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means within a vessel, so these pieces go inside

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
the tench is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Smells of fish begin to leak out on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stenches are strong, foul smells; a whiff is a smell too, usually unpleasant.

clue.text: Class hasn't finished eating most of old pudding

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside
not finished means the final letter is missing

parts.note: a seminar is a teaching class

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A school class leaves some of its old dessert uneaten.
explanation.walkthrough: SEMINA(R) and OL(D) each lose their last letter, then SEMINA wraps around OL.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is a milk pudding made from durum wheat grains, a school dinner classic.

clue.text: Instrument displaying pressure change in case of seismicity

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: in places the change within the shell
the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters of the word
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A seismograph registers a pressure shift during an earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument, plucked like a zither, mentioned in the Psalms.

clue.text: Patron's complaint about new leading lady

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the complaint wraps round the next item

parts.note: beef is slang for a grievance
N is the abbreviation for new
a leading lady is the star actress of a show

explanation.surface: A theatre's patron grumbles about the new star of the production.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactress is a woman who supports a cause or person with money, i.e. a female patron.

clue.text: Treatment for the ear, face and heart of lion

indicators.note: something meant for the ear is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: phiz is old slang for the face

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the two central letters

explanation.surface: A vet's remedy for a lion's ear, face and heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's first syllable is spoken fizz, the same as phiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Physio is short for physiotherapy, a course of exercise and massage used as treatment for injuries.

clue.text: Rang up policy section about dispute

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, read backwards
a section is a portion cut from a longer run of text

parts.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Someone phoned to argue about part of a company policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppugn is to call into question or argue against, an old verb meaning to contest or dispute.

clue.text: Game youngsters enjoy drink on short flight

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another is placed after it, so the drink comes second

parts.note: a hop is a brief journey by air
Scotch is whisky

explanation.surface: Children enjoy a game and a drink on a quick plane trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a playground game of hopping through chalked squares, played mostly by children.

clue.text: Hill showing a kind of lily every now and again

indicators.note: now and again means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: odd letters, starting from the k

explanation.surface: A hillside where a certain type of lily appears now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded mound or hillock, a synonym for a low hill.

clue.text: King, lacking experience, banishing just the one scoundrel

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: banishing means sending away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: naive means inexperienced
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An inexperienced king exiles a single villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A knave is a dishonest rogue, an old word for a scoundrel, and also the jack in cards.

clue.text: Cause ground to dip

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something makes the land sink down.
explanation.walkthrough: Ground looks like the noun for earth but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce can be a dip, a liquid accompaniment into which food is dunked.

clue.text: Musical rushed without Romeo's back story

indicators.note: going back means the whole assembled string is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the first words go round the last one

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, to rush
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musical about Romeo was rushed through, without its backstory.
explanation.walkthrough: EVITA RAN surrounds the R, giving EVITARRAN, which is then read backwards to give NARRATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of connected events, a synonym for a story.

clue.text: Reason not to write copy one in pen?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: nought plus the stuff a pen needs, so there is nothing to write with
second meaning: imitate the animal kept in a sty by making its grunt

explanation.surface: A writer gives an excuse for not producing copy with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as O (nothing) + INK: having nought ink is a reason not to write. The pen is a pig sty, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunt of a pig, so making it imitates an animal kept in a sty; zero ink stops any writing.

clue.text: What's left after Scotland's last energy commission

indicators.note: last points to the closing letter of the country's name

parts.note: final letter of the name
E is the physics symbol for energy
a legacy is what is left in a will

explanation.surface: Asks what remains for Scotland once its last energy reserves are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: After here is the charade signal: the legacy is placed after the other two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegacy is a body of delegates appointed to act for others, i.e. a commission or committee.
